claims.text: An amino acid has a central carbon atom bonded to four things: an amino group (–NH2), a carboxyl group (–COOH), a hydrogen atom and an R group. The R group differs from one amino acid to another, and about twenty different amino acids are used to build the proteins of living organisms.

claims.text: Two amino acids join by a condensation reaction between the carboxyl group of one and the amino group of the other: an –OH from the carboxyl group and an H from the amino group leave as a molecule of water, and a peptide bond (C–N) forms between the carbon and the nitrogen. Two amino acids joined in this way make a dipeptide, and many make a polypeptide.

claims.text: Haemoglobin is a globular protein: a compact, roughly spherical molecule of four polypeptide chains (two alpha-globin and two beta-globin) held together as its quaternary structure. Non-polar R groups point into the interior and polar R groups lie on the outside, which makes the molecule soluble in the cytoplasm of a red blood cell. Each chain holds one haem group, so one molecule has four.
